title: Graceful dual-region session migration and streaming fallback for hosted gateway
creator: Marco Alvarez
description: Problem: Hosted API customers experience intermittent cross-region degradations (network partitions, regional GPU congestion). We need a failover model that preserves session/streaming semantics for in-flight connections (websocket/HTTP streaming) while satisfying tenant SLOs and minimizing token cost and user-visible errors. This ticket defines a pragmatic dual-region migration strategy with transparent traffic shifting, streaming fallback mode, circuit breaker integration, and load-shedding knobs for overload scenarios.
acceptance_criteria:
1) New gateway flows can shift traffic between primary and secondary regions for a tenant without requiring client reconnection for short handovers (<=30s grace window).
2) For streaming sessions, implement a fallback that resumes from last acknowledged token when possible, or gracefully completes with a clear error and metrics when not.
3) Circuit-breaker state machine integrates with per-tenant SLOs and can trigger selective load shedding (non-critical routes first).
4) End-to-end tests (integration + chaos) validate that 99% of requests for targeted tenants meet P99 latency SLOs during a simulated regional flapping event.
5) Dashboards surfaced in Console: per-tenant failover events, stream-resume success rate, circuit-breaker triggers, and dropped-token metrics.
6) Runbook updated with step-by-step rollback and escalation paths.
design_decisions:
- Use a dual-active routing table per tenant: primary region + prioritized fallback list.
- For short-lived streaming sessions (<2 minutes) attempt transparent in-band handover using proxy-level buffered tail packets and token-level checkpointing (kv-cache snapshot).
- For long-running streams, prefer a deterministic graceful shutdown: send STREAM_PAUSE event to client SDK via SSE/frame and mark session migratable; if client reconnects within grace window it attempts resume with session ID and last acked token.
- Circuit breaker is tiered: local per-worker CB (fast failure on overload) + regional CB aggregated by gateway (trips based on sustained error/latency percentiles and queue length).
- Load shedding policy: drop or downgrade low-priority routes (embeddings batch jobs, background reranks) before terminating live chat generation.
- Traffic shifting algorithm: weighted gradual shift with sigmoid ramp over 60s by default, with emergency immediate cut to fallback if safety limits are hit.
- Telemetry contract: all handover attempts emit events with reason, duration, session id, resume result, and fallback model variant used.
implementation_plan:
1) Runtime: implement session checkpoint API (kv-cache snapshot + model position) and make it pluggable to the gateway.
2) Gateway: add per-tenant routing table and shift controller; expose config flags to PM and SRE.
3) Streaming layer: implement STREAM_PAUSE/RESUME wire frames and SDK helpers (js/python) to attempt resume.
4) Circuit breakers: hook runtime latency and token-queue metrics to CB engine; expose thresholds as tenant-configurable.
5) Load shedding: implement priority tags on routes and scheduler-level preemption.
6) Tests: unit + integration + chaos harness against simulated region outage.
7) Docs: Console doc pages and runbook.
Implementation owners: Priya (gateway & routing), Liam Chen (streaming layer & SDK), Sofia Martinez (CB & scheduler), Marco (telemetry & dashboards).
Milestones: a) API + gateway prototype (2 wks), b) streaming resume + SDK (3 wks), c) CB integration + load shedding (2 wks), d) E2E tests and rollout (1 wk).
rollout_plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): enable for internal staging tenants only. Monitor stream-resume success and P99 latency.
- Phase 2 (pilot): enable for 3 low-risk customers with high availability needs; run extended chaos (simulated latency spikes, region partition) for 72h.
- Phase 3 (regional opt-in): allow tenants to opt into automatic failover via Console; default off for customers with active regulatory constraints.
- Phase 4 (global): flip default to on for new tenants after 8 weeks of stable pilot metrics.
Controls: kill-switch per-tenant, region-wide emergency revert with 30s abort window.
Communication: pre-rollout notes to SRE, Support, and Sales; blog post with guidance for customers integrating SDK resume flows.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for checkpoint serialization and resume idempotency.
- Integration: gateway + runtime resume under simulated tail-loss.
- Chaos tests: orchestrate AWS/GCP region-level network blackholes and CPU starvation; verify failover logic within safety thresholds.
- Performance: benchmark mem/CPU overhead with kv-cache snapshots under 10k concurrent streams.
- Regression: ensure no change to non-streaming request latencies (<=5% delta p50/p95).
- Acceptance thresholds: stream-resume success >= 85% for short handovers; overall customer-visible error rate increase <= 0.5% during failover windows.
telemetry:
Required metrics and traces to add:
- gateway.failover.attempts (tags: tenant, from_region, to_region, reason)
- gateway.failover.success_rate (tenant)
- stream.resume.attempts, stream.resume.success, stream.resume.latency
- cb.tripped.count, cb.tripped.duration, cb.scope (worker/region/tenant)
- scheduler.shed.count (route_priority)
- session.kv_snapshot.size, session.kv_snapshot.duration
- trace samples including checkpoint hash and last_ack_token
Dashboards: Failover Overview, Streaming Reliability, Circuit Breaker Heatmap, Load-shedding trends.
Alerts: cb.tripped.rate > 10/min for >5m -> page SRE; stream.resume.success_rate < 60% for >15m -> P1 ops.
risks:
- Resume correctness: some model internals (non-deterministic sampling, stateful decoders) may make exact resume impossible leading to duplicate tokens or incoherence. Mitigation: detect non-resumable models and fall back to explicit reconnect with user-visible error.
- Cost: additional kv snapshots and buffering increase memory and network usage; will need quota and throttles for snapshot frequency.
- Complexity: SDK changes required for best-effort resume may slow adoption; provide server-side graceful fallback.
- Edge-case: long-running streams crossing region boundaries with different model variants may degrade quality; add model-variant compatibility checks before migration.
- Security: session IDs and snapshots must be encrypted and access controlled; coordinate with Security for KMS integration (see dependencies).
